  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video,

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  April 23, 2024

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  April 23, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
  of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member Morales.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager/ Acting Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Jose Cortes  Assistant City Manager
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
  on the Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Faulk, and seconded by Council
  Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated April 19, 2024,
  in the amount of $4,245,500.97, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/
  Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Morales.

301  RESOLUTION NO. 24-52 ADOPTED – APPROVAL OF THE FINAL TRACT MAP
  NO. 82105 TO ALLOW A 20-UNIT RESIDENTIAL TOWNHOME SUBDIVISION
  ON A 28,343 SQUARE-FOOT R-3/P-1 (MULTIPLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL/
  AUTOMOBILE PARKING) ZONED PROPERTY LOCATED AT 113-133
  PLYMOUTH STREET. Staff report dated April 23, 2024, was presented recommending
  that the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution approving Final Tract Map No.
  82105 to allow a 20-unit residential townhouse subdivision on a 28,343 square-foot R-3/P-
  1 (Multiple-Family Residential/Automobile Parking) Zoned property at 113-133 Plymouth
  Street.
 April 23, 2024

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 24-52 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING FINAL TRACT MAP NO.
  82105 TO ALLOW A 20-UNIT RESIDENTIAL TOWNHOME
  SUBDIVISION ON A 28,343 SQUARE-FOOT R-3/P-1 (MULTIPLE-
  FAMILY RESIDENTIAL/ AUTOMOBILE PARKING) ZONED
  PROPERTY AT 113-133 PLYMOUTH STREET

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

183  FACILITIES RELOCATION AGREEMENT NO. 24-201 APPROVED – CROWN
  CASTLE. Staff report dated April 23, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor
  and Council Members approve a Facilities Relocation Agreement with Crown Castle for
  the ITC Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that the
  City Council does hereby approve Facilities Relocation Agreement No. 24-201. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

183  AMENDMENT NO. 4 TO AGREEMENT NO. 22-011 – TERRY A. HAYES
  ASSOCIATES, INC.; RESOLUTION NO. 24-53 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report dated April 23, 2024,
  was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve Amendment
  No. 4 to Agreement No. 22-011 with Terry A. Hayes Associates Inc., for Environmental
  Documentation and Technical Studies for the Inglewood Transit Connector Project (ITC)
  for an additional amount of $45,047 (total contract amount not to exceed $1,011,080).

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that the
  City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 4 to Agreement No. 22-011; and 2)
  Adopt Resolution No. 24-53 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2023-24 BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson reported on her
  attendance at the AKA Event, along with Councilwoman Faulk. She thanked and
  congratulated Councilwoman Faulk on her event and said she saw the KIA Forum light
  up in pink and green. She also reported on her attendance at the STEM Fest, along with
  the Mayor, and stated it was fantastic seeing all the children there. She thanked Thomas Uwal,
  Parks and Recreation Director, Teresa Estrada, Recreation Superintendent, and Daniel
  Medina, Senior Recreation Leader. Finally, she expressed her excitement about the  Women
  Rock Empowerment Summit and looked forward to seeing all the women and the fantastic
  presenters.

  2
 April 23, 2024

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the memory of Pastor Cecil “Chip” Murray, and Kimberly Murray, mother of
  Mia Walker, at the hour of 2:14 p.m.

  Approved this ___ day of _______, 2024.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
